A2A² LEARNING STUDIO

CM3400 / CM6600 · Course Project

One project, six parts — climbing Bloom's taxonomy

Across this course project you'll build a complete construction risk register — one piece at a time, over six connected parts. Each part is a module, and each asks more of you than the last: you climb Bloom's taxonomy, from understanding risks, to creating the plans that control them, all the way to communicating the whole story the way a project manager briefs an owner.

Understand
Part 1 · IDENTIFY · Module 2 — classify each risk into one of six families and frame it as cause → event → consequence, with an owner and a trigger. (you're here)
Analyze
Part 2 · COMPOUND · Module 3 — expand each risk into its cause-and-effect network: the parallel causes and consequences a real risk carries.
Evaluate
Part 3 · ASSESS · Module 4 — rate each risk's probability and impact across the build phases, then score (P × I) and band its severity.
Create
Part 4 · RESPOND · Module 5 — choose a response for every cause and consequence — avoid, reduce, transfer, or accept — and design the action that delivers it.
Create +
Part 5 · CONTROL · Module 6 — build a stage-by-stage control plan that holds each risk in check from pre-contract through closeout.
Communicate
Part 6 · NARRATE · Module 7 — write a two-page risk-and-safety narrative the way a PM briefs an owner: name your highest-banded risks, their liability and insurance exposure — bonds, builder's risk, CGL, contractual transfer — and the mitigation that protects the completion date, every claim cited to its register code.

Your work carries forward — the risks you identify in Part 1 are the very ones you'll analyze, score, respond to, control, and finally narrate to the owner in the parts ahead. A careful Part 1 sets up the whole project.

CM3400 / CM6600 · The case study

The Midtown MOB Risk Register

You've just joined the General Contractor's pre-construction risk team for the Midtown Medical Office Building (MOB) — a fast-track, Design–Bid–Build job in suburban Atlanta: a 6-story medical office and parking deck on a tight infill site, right next to active clinics. The owner is Midtown Health Partners, and the tenant move-in date is fixed.

Before a shovel hits the ground, your team has to see the risks coming — the things that could blow the budget, slip the schedule, or hurt someone — and put a plan around them. Learning to do that, deliberately and early, is exactly what this project trains you for.

Why do this before breaking ground? The cheapest — and safest — time to deal with a risk is before it happens. Catch it early, plan for it, and the whole job runs smoother. That habit is the heart of construction risk management, and it's what this project builds.

The project at a glance

The building6-story medical office + 2-level parking deck · 145,000 SF.
OwnerMidtown Health Partners — a private healthcare developer.
Budget$58 M · GMP target set after bid leveling.
DeliveryDesign–Bid–Build, fast-track — early steel & long-lead MEP packages.
Schedule18 months from notice to proceed, to a fixed tenant move-in date.
Site & limitsTight suburban-Atlanta infill by active clinics; noise/dust & work-hour limits, tight laydown, permit-sensitive.

Walk the job site

These are the ten scenes on the Midtown MOB — the actual site you'll be reading. In Part 1 you study them to spot and classify risks, and Jack Mo points you to the right scene for each row. Click any photo to enlarge.

In Part 1 · IDENTIFY you'll build your five rows of the team's shared risk register: classify the risks you're handed, and find new ones by reading the site photos.

Getting started

Which semester, class, Group and Team-member ID do I pick?

Exactly what's posted in D2L: your semester and year, your class code (W sections are online), and your Group + Team-member ID from the group file. Your work saves under this full identity and your instructor grades by it. Every download (backup, Excel) records all of it — including your PIN — so you can always recover what you picked. Wrong seat? Part 1 → ↻ change team member and fix it before you do real work.

What is the PIN for? What if I forget it?

The PIN protects your ID on a shared or lab computer, so another student can't open your work under your name. You create it the first time you enter. Forgot it? Restore your own backup file (⬆ Restore .json at the bottom) — that reclaims your ID — or ask your instructor. Tip: on the identity page, press ⬇ Save my ID card — it downloads everything you picked, including the PIN you typed.

Someone else's work shows up when I open the app.

You're on a shared computer and the last student didn't switch out. Go to Part 1 → ↻ change team member, pick your own Group and ID, and enter. Your own progress — including which part you were on — comes back with it.

The Part 2–5 tabs are locked.

That's the design: each part unlocks when you submit the one before it. Finish and submit Part 1, and Part 2 opens (once its module is open in D2L too).

Working through the parts

What am I doing in each part?

Part 1 · IDENTIFY — build your five risk rows (cause → event → consequence, plus category, owner, trigger). Part 2 · COMPOUND — give each risk 3 parallel causes and 3 parallel effects. Part 3 · ASSESS — rate every row 1–5 in each project phase; score and band calculate themselves. Part 4 · RESPOND — choose a response type, action, and residual for every row, driven by the ratings. Part 5 · CONTROL — audit the auto-calculated stage-by-stage control plan, and change any stage you can defend.

The first rows are frozen and I can't edit them.

Those are worked examples — model answers to learn from. Read them, copy the thinking, then do your own rows (marked your turn). Your last risk has no worked rows at all: that one is fully yours.

The dropdown doesn't have the answer I want.

For the subjective cells (cause, event, consequence, parallels, response actions) scroll to the bottom of the dropdown and pick ✍ Write my own… — type your wording and it goes into the cell. The analysis will mark it "your own wording": it can't check it against the scene, so be ready to defend it.

Why does the dropdown go blank after I pick something?

By design — your chosen value shows as the cell text, and the dropdown stays empty, ready for a re-pick. To change an answer, just pick again. ↩ Undo steps back through this session.

In Part 5, can I change what the grid calculated?

Yes — that's the point. Click any stage and set the truer state. Your change keeps an orange ring and Run analysis will ask you to defend it. A changed stage is fine; an unexplained one is not.

Voice guides & Jack Mo

What are the ▶ buttons on the rows?

Each risk row has its own voice guide — it walks you through exactly that row's job, lighting up each thing it talks about. The green banner at the top plays a tour of the whole page. Start every part by playing them.

The voice guide doesn't play / has no sound.

Click somewhere on the page first (browsers block audio before the first click), check your volume and tab-mute (right-click the browser tab), and try again. Still silent? Reload the page — your work is saved.

Who is Jack Mo and what can I ask him?

Jack Mo is the project's AI project manager — scan the QR at the top of the page (or use its link). Ask him about the project: causes, ratings, response logic, "is my reasoning sound?". He coaches with questions; he will never fill a cell for you, and platform questions (saving, submitting) belong here, not with him.

Saving, backups & moving computers

Where is my work saved?

Automatically, on every change — to D2L when you launched from there, otherwise to this browser on this computer. The "✓ saved to…" note at the bottom tells you which. Browser saves live in that browser on that computer — use the SAME browser on the SAME computer all semester. Don't work in incognito/private mode, and don't clear cookies / site data (that erases saved work; clearing history alone is harmless). Switching computers = restore your backup file.

How do I move my work to another computer?

⬇ Backup (.json) on computer A, then ⬆ Restore (.json) on computer B. The backup carries everything — all parts, your progress, your ID. A backup also downloads automatically every time you submit a part.

I lost my work!

First: same computer, same browser, same Group + Team-member ID? Enter those and it should reappear. If not, ⬆ Restore your latest backup .json (check your Downloads folder — every submit saved one automatically). That file is your safety net.

Run analysis & submitting

Run analysis flagged my answer — is it wrong?

Not necessarily. The analysis checks your work against the scene and the method rules, and flags what looks off — as a question, not a verdict. If you can defend your answer, you may keep it; you'll confirm before submitting. Click any flagged item to jump to its cell.

Can I change answers after submitting a part?

You can still edit, and your latest state goes with each later part's submission and exports — but the recorded action report for a part is written when you submit it. Treat submit as "done with this part."

What exactly is graded?

Each submitted part records a completion point plus a full action report — every answer you gave and what the analysis said — to D2L (or into your backup file). Your instructor sees process, not just answers.

What are the Excel / Backup buttons at the bottom?

⬇ Excel (.xlsx) — your whole register so far, every part, in the same layout as the group register file. ⬇ Backup (.json) / ⬆ Restore (.json) — your save file. Everything also auto-downloads at each submit.

Troubleshooting

The page looks cut off / I have to scroll sideways.

The register is wide by design. On a smaller screen, scroll horizontally inside the table, or zoom the browser out one step (Ctrl + minus).

A popup (photo, matrix, worked example) won't open.

Click the cell or button once and wait a moment — the photos are full-resolution. If it's stuck, reload the page; your work is saved.

Something else is broken.

Reload first — your work is saved on every change. If it persists, take a screenshot of what you see, note your Group + ID and which part/row, and send it to your instructor.
